Worst case: someone saw him leave, there's a camera, the owner files a police report, and now he's looking at criminal charges on top of everything else.

So here's what I'd think about. What does your brother actually remember from last night? Where was he really? If you're going to set up a story, it needs to be simple and consistent — because if he gets one detail wrong under pressure, someone's going to notice.

The right thing is probably not lying. The right thing is probably sitting down with your brother when he's sober and clear-headed, looking at the damage honestly, and making a plan together. Maybe that plan involves coming forward. Maybe it involves talking to a lawyer first. Maybe it involves having your parents help.

But the one thing I'd really encourage you not to do is let him spiral alone. Panic is what made him drive off in the first place. What he needs now is someone steady next to him.

Okay. Let's slow down. Here's a step by step that feels honest and safe.

**First thing — check the damage.** Go with your brother to look at the other car if you can find it. How bad is it? Scratch vs. dent vs. actual mechanical damage? This changes everything about what happens next.

**Second thing — do NOT say anything to anyone yet.** No insurance companies, no police, no social media posts. The second this gets reported, the clock starts ticking in a direction you can't control.

**Third thing — talk to your parents.** I know that's terrifying. But they need to know before someone else tells them. And honestly? Parents who are angry but informed can help in ways you can't. They might have connections, a lawyer, relationships that smooth things over.

**Fourth thing — if the damage is minor and no one has reported it yet, your brother could actually go back to the scene and come forward himself.** That looks incredibly different from driving off. It shows responsibility. A scholarship committee would see that.

**Fifth — get him to a lawyer.** Even a quick consultation. Just to understand what he's actually looking at legally.
